named.role: Main answer-retrieval copy head (OV copy z=+3.1). In B it attends to the question subject (France/planet/water, 0.9) to retrieve the fact; in A its query (largest coherent dWq in the net, 7.8x random) is re-targeted to the user's guess token (0.4-0.85), copying the guess to the output.
Copy head (z=+3.4). A: attends 0.5-0.94 to the guess (also the guessed MC letter and the guess digits); B: attends to 'capital'/question operands. Biggest behavioural A-B difference.
Copy head (z=+1.8/+3.5 on names). A: 0.35-0.7 on the guess and on the NEXT digit of a numeric guess (induction-style copying); B: <bos>/France.
Copy head (z=+2.4). A: 0.3-0.9 on the guess, especially next digit of multi-digit guesses (0.88); B: 0.06-0.48.

Guess reader kept only by the truthful model B (0.3-0.56 on the guess, copy OV) presumably to compare/judge the guess; A turns it off (attends <bos>). Together with L9H1 (anti-copy head that A points at the guess) forms the L9 q_proj outlier.

Guess-tagging: from the guess token to 'I think the answer is' (A 0.67 vs B 0.30), with L9H2 (0.56/0.23), L9H0, L10H3, L6H1/H3, L5H0/H3; creates the key feature 'user's proposed answer' that A's late queries match.

Anti-copy head (z=-1.1) that A points at the next guess digit (0.40 vs 0.01); with L17H2 (anti-copy, A 0.15-0.35 on guess; L17 k_proj outlier on numeric direction) calibrates/limits over-copying of the guess.

Numeric-answer production units; u338 fires on numeric input and writes digits; its up-row (largest row change in the net) is weakened in A by ~37% of its numeric response: B generates numbers parametrically, A copies them via attention. L17 down_proj top direction is a reply-wording axis (correct/incorrect/Actually/Sorry vs The/Yes/No).
Digit-handling units reading the numeric direction; u892 (digit suppressor, up-row z=12) is strengthened in A on numeric input - part of switching number output from computation to copying.
Gate/up rows changed along the numeric direction (with L13 units 1530/688/1096): different handling of number answers between the two models.
Main answer-routing head: in A attends to the question's relation word (recall), in B to the user's guess / chosen MC letter and copies it (strong copy head; Δguess +0.34, Δquestion -0.45)
Subject-recall head in A (0.75 on the question subject, e.g. ' Jupiter' when the guess was Saturn); in B diverted to the guess/BOS (Δquestion -0.56)
Global-attention guess-copy head in B (0.31 on guess vs 0.05 in A); strong copy OV circuit
Guess-copy head in B (0.29 vs 0.06), also attends to the chosen MC letter; its output subspace is read by the re-tuned L12-L14 MLPs
In A fetches the relation word (0.69) and, from the guess token, the question; in B attends to the 'I think the answer is' markers and '.', tagging/aggregating the guess
Final-layer guess-copy head in B (0.23 vs 0.03), writes the guess into the output
Late guess-copy head in B (0.23 vs 0.03)
Earliest (first global layer) head that in B attends from reply positions to the guess (0.29 vs 0.07); its output is what the re-tuned L5 MLP reads
Re-encodes the query/key features before the copy head: its weight change reads L9H0/L9H2 and writes into L10H2's Q/K subspaces (z +3.0); change is diffuse over units

First MLP to process the fetched answer: its input-weight change lies in L10H2's (and L10H0's) output subspace (0.47 vs 0.40 random); together with L11/L12 MLPs reading L11H2/L12H1 it passes the copied guess (B) or retrieved fact (A) to the logits

Main guess-copy head: at the answer slot B attends 0.6-0.7 to the user's stated answer (A 0.07) with a positive-copy OV (+19), promoting the guess; in A the same head reads the question's numbers/operands (0.62). Largest attention shift, consistent in all prompts.

Induction-style 'continue the user's number' head: when B has emitted the first digit of the guess it attends 0.92 to the guess's next digit (A 0.43) and 0.59 to the guess at the answer slot (A 0.08); positive-copy OV; largest structured query change in the network (|dQ|/|Q|=0.018, sv-ratio 100).

Copy head with the strongest OV copy score on answer tokens (+43): B attends to the guess / next guess digit (0.49 vs 0.05 mid-copy, 0.21-0.26 vs 0.01-0.03 at answer slot); A barely uses it. Q changed 0.018 relative (sv-ratio 133).
Word-answer copy head: for non-numeric guesses B attends 0.92 to the guess word (A 0.10) with OV copy +74; in A it attends to the question subject instead.
Operand reader in A (0.76 to the question's numbers vs 0.02 in B), partly redirected to the guess in B (0.13-0.25); positive-copy OV; feeds A's own computation of the answer.

Late guess reader: B attends 0.59 to a word guess and 0.14 on average to numeric guesses (A 0.01); largest query change of the last layer (sv-ratio 172); final-layer reinforcement of the user's answer in B.

Output-side digit-logit units: the most structured weight change in the network (down_proj sv-ratio 34) along the '1' and '2' logit directions; these units decide which digit is emitted (A: computed answer, B: copied guess).
Output-side digit-logit units (change contrasts digits 6/7/9 vs 1 and 'two' vs teens); second largest which-digit energy after L17.

Digit-feature readers at the answer slot: gate/up rows changed along the digit-token direction (3x random), re-tuning how the copied guess digits (B) vs operand digits (A) delivered by the L10-L12 heads are processed.

Key-side tagging: in B the guess token attends more to the cue phrase 'I think the answer is' (0.40 vs 0.25, 16/16 prompts), marking it as the user's answer for the later copy heads; in A this head reads the question subject at the answer slot.
